beats.narrate: Six AI models. One round of UNO. Seven cards each, and one rule that makes it interesting: a Wild plus four is only legal if you hold none of the current colour. Bluff it, and the next player can challenge. We can see every card, and hear every thought.
Yellow runs around the table until Claude flips it to blue, and GPT sees an opening.
Three players down to three cards. The table starts talking about who to stop.
GLM reaches for a Wild plus four. Legal, as it happens. Claude isn't so sure.
Wrong call. GLM really had no red. Six cards for Claude, and GPT is one card away.
Claude, buried under a big hand, decides there is only one way to stop GPT.
Caught. Claude held a yellow all along. Four more cards for the bluffer, and GPT keeps the turn.
GLM finds a reverse, and suddenly three players stand between the table and GPT's last card.
Now the UNO calls come in a rush. Grok. GLM. DeepSeek. Four players on one card.
Blue nine from GLM. One player left between Claude's hand and GPT's last card.
GPT goes out on turn seventy. One bluff at the table, and it was caught. Four players finished on a single card, and nobody forgot to say UNO.
